title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: love of justice requires no one be loved in Christ unto actual fruitful share of salvation before persevering faith — yet may be loved unto eternal preparation of salvation before being considered as believing
latin: Ut in pauca contraham responsionem nostram, dico, Amorem justitiae requirere ut nemo in Christo ad salutem ametur, nisi qui fide ipsum apprehenderit; sed hoc sensu, ut minime ametur ad actualem et fructuosam participationem salutis priusquam in fide perseveraverit, amari tamen possit ad aeternam salutis in mente et voluntate Divina preparationem priusquam consideretur ut credens et in hac fide perseverans. Nam ipsa praeparatio fidei et perseverantiae sunt amoris Divini argumenta: praeparantur autem prius quam infallibiliter praevidentur in Petro infallibiliter futurae. Atque praeparantur haec dona salutifera singularibus personis infallibiliter conferenda, non nisi ex amore ad salutem illorum spectante. Neque in hac praeparatione Deus violare putandus est leges justitiae suae, sed explicare opes specialis misericordiae suae.
pass_a: That I may contract our response into few words, I say that the love of justice requires that no one be loved in Christ unto salvation, unless he who by faith has apprehended him; but in this sense, that he by no means be loved unto the actual and fruitful participation of salvation before he shall have persevered in faith, yet he can be loved unto the everlasting preparation of salvation in the Divine mind and will before he be considered as believing and persevering in this faith. For the very preparation of faith and of perseverance are arguments of Divine love: but they are prepared before they are infallibly foreseen in Peter as infallibly about to be. And these saving gifts are prepared to be infallibly conferred upon singular persons, not except from a love looking unto their salvation. Nor in this preparation is God to be thought to violate the laws of his justice, but to unfold the riches of his special mercy.
pass_b: To put our answer in few words: love of justice requires that no one be loved in Christ unto salvation unless he has apprehended him by faith. Take that in this sense: he is not loved unto actual fruitful share of salvation before he has persevered in faith — yet he can be loved unto the eternal preparation of salvation in God's mind and will before he is considered as believing and persevering in that faith. For the very preparation of faith and perseverance are marks of divine love: they are prepared before they are infallibly foreseen in Peter as infallibly about to be. And these saving gifts are prepared to be infallibly conferred on singular persons only from a love that looks to their salvation. In that preparation God is not to be thought to violate the laws of his justice, but to unfold the riches of his special mercy.

lemmas.gloss: loved unto preparation before considered as believing
preparation unfolds mercy, does not violate justice

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: Arminius's further scruple — loving some unto salvation before Christ was ordained Mediator to expiate sins equals loving sinners more than justice
latin: Sed alter scrupulus hic eximendus est. Urget Arminius, nos ponere Deum non modo amare quosdam ad salutem ante praevisam fidem et obedientiam eorundem, sed antequam Christus sit ordinatus ut sua obedientia peccata expiaret; quia docemus Christum ideo fuisse datum in Mediatorem, quia Deus decreverat servare electos: quod perinde est ac si dicamus, Deum magis amasse homines peccatores, quam suam justitiam.
pass_a: But another scruple is here to be removed. Arminius urges that we place God as loving certain ones unto salvation not only before their foreseen faith and obedience, but before Christ was ordained that by his obedience he should expiate sins; because we teach that Christ was therefore given as Mediator, because God had decreed to save the elect: which is as if we should say that God loved sinful men more than his own justice.
pass_b: But another scruple must be cleared here. Arminius urges that we set God as loving some unto salvation not only before their foreseen faith and obedience, but before Christ was ordained to expiate sins by his obedience — because we teach that Christ was given as Mediator because God had decreed to save the elect. That, he says, is as if we said God loved sinful men more than his own justice.

lemmas.gloss: charged with loving sinners over justice

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: priority of Mediator-decree vs elect-saving decree is hard speculation — execution-order is clear; eternal conception-order only God knows
latin: Haec argutatio vocat nos ad speculationem valde difficilem, et dogmaticae Theologiae fundandae minime accommodatam. Nicitur enim consideratione Prioritatis et Posterioritatis in illis duobus voluntatis Divinae decretis, de dando Mediatore, et de electis servandis, quae utraque ab aeterno fuerunt concepta et constituta. Ad me quod attinet, scio ordinem exsecutionis, secundum quem Deus voluit beneficia ad homines pervenire, nullo negotio posse delineari: at quo ordine Deus ea consignata tenuit ab aeterno in mente ac voluntate sua, is solus enarrare praesumat qui se Deo ab arcanis et aeternis consiliis fuisse etiam affirmare audeat.
pass_a: This argumentation calls us unto a speculation exceedingly difficult, and by no means fitted unto founding dogmatic Theology. For it leans upon consideration of Priority and Posteriority in those two decrees of the Divine will, concerning giving a Mediator, and concerning saving the elect, which both were conceived and established from eternity. As for what pertains unto me, I know that the order of execution, according to which God willed benefits to come unto men, can be delineated with no trouble: but in what order God held them sealed from eternity in his mind and will, let him alone presume to narrate who dares even to affirm that he has been with God from the secret and everlasting counsels.
pass_b: This argument calls us into a very hard speculation, poorly fitted to founding dogmatic theology. It hangs on priority and posteriority between those two decrees of divine will — giving a Mediator, and saving the elect — both conceived and established from eternity. As for me: I know the order of execution, by which God willed benefits to reach men, can be sketched with no trouble. But in what order he held them sealed from eternity in his mind and will — let only him presume to tell who dares claim he has been with God from the secret eternal counsels.

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: we confess execution-order — Christ first proposed, then apprehended by faith, then justification, sanctification, glorification; mapping a distinct decree-series in God's mind overtrusts wit
latin: Fatemur igitur Deum ab aeterno constituisse ut omnibus salvandis Christus primo in loco proponeretur, dein per fidem apprehenderetur, hinc ut eorundem justificatio sequeretur, tum sanctificatio, et demum glorificatio: Sed si quis minime contentus hoc ordine exsecutionis, velit etiam nobis describere seriem decretorum Divinorum, ordine conceptionis in mente ac voluntate Dei quasi distinctam, atque urgeat cum Arminio, Divinam justitiam impugnari, nisi hoc consideretur ut illo prius, is mihi videtur nimium ingenio suo fidere.
pass_a: We confess therefore that God from eternity established that unto all to be saved Christ should first in place be proposed, then be apprehended by faith, thence that their justification should follow, then sanctification, and finally glorification: But if anyone by no means content with this order of execution should also wish to describe unto us a series of the Divine decrees, in the order of conception in the mind and will of God as it were distinct, and should urge with Arminius that the Divine justice is impugned unless this be considered as prior to that, he seems unto me to trust his own wit too much.
pass_b: So we confess that from eternity God established this for all who are to be saved: Christ first proposed, then apprehended by faith, then their justification, then sanctification, and at last glorification. But if anyone, not content with that order of execution, also wants to map for us a distinct series of divine decrees in the order of conception in God's mind and will, and with Arminius urges that divine justice is attacked unless one decree is set prior to the other — he seems to me to trust his own wit too much.

lemmas.gloss: execution-order: Christ, faith, justification, sanctification, glory
overtrusting wit to rank eternal decrees

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: first knot — Vasquez: even if Christ ordered after predestination, in execution Christ's merit causes every predestination-effect; intending a sinner's salvation with means that first satisfy justice is mercy, not loving the sinner more than justice
latin: Quod igitur objectum fuit, labefactari Divinam justitiam, si ponamus Deum prius elegisse quosdam ad vitam, quam ordinaverit Christum ad expianda peccata, hic scrupulus dissolvi potest. Primo, si quis cum subtili Doctore respondeat, Utcunque Christus Christique merita erga homines ordinata fuerunt post praedestinationem, tamen cum in exsecutione meritum Christi sit causa cujuscunque effectus a praedestinatione manantis, nihil fit contra justitiam Dei in salute electorum. Nam ex mera misericordia intendere salutem alicujus peccatoris, atque ex hac intentione providere illi talia media, ut hoc minime fiat priusquam justitiae fuerit satisfactum, non est peccatorem magis amare quam justitiam, sed velle exercere gratuitam misericordiam erga peccatorem, potius quam debitam justitiam.
pass_a: What therefore was objected — that the Divine justice is shaken, if we place God as having first elected certain ones unto life before he ordained Christ unto expiating sins — this scruple can be dissolved. First, if anyone with the subtle Doctor answer, Howsoever Christ and the merits of Christ toward men were ordained after predestination, yet since in execution the merit of Christ is the cause of whatsoever effect flowing from predestination, nothing is done against the justice of God in the salvation of the elect. For of mere mercy to intend the salvation of some sinner, and from this intention to provide him such media that this by no means be done before justice shall have been satisfied, is not to love the sinner more than justice, but to will to exercise gratuitous mercy toward the sinner, rather than due justice.
pass_b: So the objection that divine justice is shaken if we set God as electing some to life before ordaining Christ to expiate sins — that scruple can be loosed. First, with the subtle Doctor: however Christ and his merits toward men were ordered after predestination, yet in execution Christ's merit is the cause of every effect flowing from predestination — so nothing is done against God's justice in the elect's salvation. Of mere mercy to intend a sinner's salvation, and from that intention to provide him such means that it is never done before justice is satisfied, is not to love the sinner more than justice — it is to will to exercise free mercy toward the sinner rather than due justice.

lemmas.lemma: meritum Christi ... causa ... effectus a praedestinatione
lemmas.gloss: Vasquez: Christ's merit causes predestination-effects in execution

lemmas.lemma: gratuitam misericordiam ... potius quam debitam justitiam
lemmas.gloss: mercy with means that satisfy justice first

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: second knot — Biel: do not posit priorities (or plural ordered acts) among these divine decrees; ranking incarnation before/after election is false speculation
latin: Secundo nodus iste discindi potest, si quis cum Biele defendat, Prioritates illas in Divinis hisce decretis non esse ponendas, sicut nec pluralitates actuum ordinatorum; ac proinde si quis considerare velit talem ordinem horum decretorum ut ponat Christi incarnationem electione priorem, vel e contra, hanc considerationem esse falsam speculationem. Sic Biel, in 3. dist. 2. qu. dub. 3.
pass_a: Secondly this knot can be cut, if anyone with Biel defend that those Priorities are not to be placed in these Divine decrees, as neither pluralities of ordered acts; and accordingly if anyone should wish to consider such an order of these decrees as places the incarnation of Christ prior to election, or on the contrary, that this consideration is false speculation. So Biel, in 3. dist. 2. qu. dub. 3.
pass_b: Second, this knot can be cut with Biel: those priorities are not to be set among these divine decrees — nor pluralities of ordered acts. So if anyone wants to consider an order of these decrees that sets Christ's incarnation before election, or the reverse, that consideration is false speculation (Biel, in 3. dist. 2. qu. dub. 3).

lemmas.gloss: Biel: no priority-ranking among these decrees

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: if we distinguish decrees by prior/posterior for weak intellect — general will to redeem via Christ (John iii. 16) and special will whereby Christ is Head of all predestined
latin: Denique, si ad sustentandam intellectus nostri imbecillitatem haec Dei decreta distinguamus secundum prius et posterius, per respectus ad objecta, quae varia et distincta sunt, arbitror nos commodissime concipere in Deo 1. voluntatem generalem redimendi humanum genus sub conditione fidei, per incarnandum Salvatorem nostrum et Mediatorem Jesum Christum; uti exprimitur Joann. iii. 16, Sic Deus dilexit mundum, etc. 2. voluntatem specialem, secundum quam Christus a Patre ordinatus Mediator constituitur Caput omnium praedestinatorum, in quo et per quem, quicquid ad gratiam et gloriam infallibiliter consequendam necessarium est, iisdem praeparandum et donandum decernitur. Hoc posito, evanescit praedicta objectio, quia Christus concipitur ut ordinatus Mediator et datus in Caput Ecclesiae, hoc est, omnium electorum, priusquam illi considerentur ut ordinati ad efficacem participationem sive gratiae sive gloriae.
pass_a: Finally, if unto sustaining the weakness of our intellect we distinguish these decrees of God according to prior and posterior, by respects unto objects which are various and distinct, I judge that we most conveniently conceive in God 1. a general will of redeeming the human race under the condition of faith, through our Savior to be incarnate and Mediator Jesus Christ; as it is expressed Joann. iii. 16, So God loved the world, etc. 2. a special will, according to which Christ ordained by the Father as Mediator is constituted Head of all the predestined, in whom and through whom whatever is necessary unto infallibly obtaining grace and glory is decreed to be prepared and given unto the same. This being posited, the aforesaid objection vanishes, because Christ is conceived as ordained Mediator and given as Head of the Church, that is, of all the elect, before they are considered as ordained unto the efficacious participation either of grace or of glory.
pass_b: Finally: if to prop up our weak intellect we distinguish these decrees of God as prior and posterior by respect to varied distinct objects, I judge we most conveniently conceive in God (1) a general will to redeem the human race under the condition of faith, through our Savior to be incarnate and Mediator Jesus Christ — as John iii. 16 expresses: So God loved the world, etc.; (2) a special will, whereby Christ ordained by the Father as Mediator is made Head of all the predestined, in whom and through whom whatever is needed for infallibly obtaining grace and glory is decreed to be prepared and given them. That posited, the objection vanishes: Christ is conceived as ordained Mediator and given as Head of the Church — that is, of all the elect — before they are considered as ordained to efficacious share of grace or glory.

lemmas.gloss: special will: Christ Head of elect before their grace/glory

title: Cap. IX Arg. 14 Sol cont.: second incommodum — precise ordaining to salvation without faith/obedience-gaze does not extinguish obedience or religious care; faith required as fruit-condition, not as election-motive (Bradwardine)
latin: Ad alteram partem objectionis jam accedo, nempe quod sententia nostra omnem obedientiae necessitatem et religionis curam extinguat, quia statuit Deum praecise aliquos ad salutem ordinasse sine fidei praecedentis, aut obedientiae nostrae intuitu: Hinc enim qui est electus concludet, non opus esse ut de praestanda obedientia multum sit solicitus. Nihil dici aut cogitari potest perversius. Nam sententia nostra negat quidem necessitatem fidei aut obedientiae praevisae in nobis tanquam motivi ad actum electionis ex parte Dei considerati; sed requirit fidem et obedientiam a nobis tanquam conditionem, ad fructum electionis, id est vitam aeternam, ex parte nostra consequendum. Qui enim docent Deum ita praedestinasse quosdam ad vitam, ut non nisi per fidem et sanctitatem eo perducantur, non negant fidei necessitatem, sed agnoscunt specialem Dei in hac fide quibusdam praeparanda et donanda misericordiam.
pass_a: Unto the other part of the objection I now come, namely that our sentence extinguishes all necessity of obedience and care of religion, because it establishes that God has precisely ordained some unto salvation without the intuit of preceding faith, or of our obedience: For hence he who is elect will conclude that there is no need that he be much solicitous concerning rendering obedience. Nothing more perverse can be said or thought. For our sentence indeed denies the necessity of faith or of obedience foreseen in us as of a motive unto the act of election considered on God's part; but it requires faith and obedience from us as a condition, unto obtaining the fruit of election, that is everlasting life, on our part. For they who teach that God so predestined certain ones unto life that they are not led thither except through faith and holiness do not deny the necessity of faith, but acknowledge the special mercy of God in preparing and giving this faith unto certain ones.
pass_b: I now take the other part of the objection: that our view extinguishes all need of obedience and care for religion, because it sets God as having precisely ordained some to salvation without any gaze on preceding faith or our obedience — so the elect will conclude he need not be much solicitous about rendering obedience. Nothing more perverse can be said or thought. Our view does deny that faith or obedience foreseen in us is necessary as a motive of the election-act considered on God's part. But it requires faith and obedience from us as a condition for obtaining on our part the fruit of election — that is, everlasting life. Those who teach that God so predestined some to life that they are led there only through faith and holiness do not deny faith's necessity — they acknowledge God's special mercy in preparing and giving that faith to certain ones.

lemmas.gloss: elect need not obey is most perverse inference
